items.name: Hash functions
items.explanation: A hash function turns any input into a fixed-size number. The same input always gives the same number, and different inputs spread across the range, which is what lets servers and keys share one number line.

assumedBy.quote: The key concept of consistent hashing is that while hash functions can accept any kind of input, their output is limited to a single unsigned integer (32, 64, or 128-bit integers depending on which hash function).

items.name: WebSockets
items.explanation: A WebSocket is a connection a browser or app opens once and keeps open, so the server can push messages without being asked each time.

assumedBy.quote: Users connect to a WebSocket and spin up a session process (a GenServer)

items.name: Semaphores
items.explanation: A semaphore hands out a fixed number of permits. A caller takes one before doing the work and returns it after, so no more than that many run at once.

assumedBy.quote: In most other languages, we could use an atomic counter to track outstanding requests and bail early if the number was too high, effectively implementing a semaphore.

items.name: Publish and subscribe
items.explanation: Senders publish a message to a topic and everyone subscribed to it receives a copy, without the sender knowing who they are.

assumedBy.quote: While Discord is rich with features, most of it boils down to pub/sub.

items.name: Circuit breakers
items.explanation: A guard that stops calling a failing service for a while, so failures do not pile up.

assumedBy.quote: We didn’t want to use a circuit breaker because we didn’t want a burst in timeouts to result in a temporary state where no attempts are made at all.
